new-task.name: Propose a new task
new-task.description: Propose a brand-new ML-Relay task. The relay agent reviews the design, then builds and measures it in phases, waiting for your reply after each one.
new-task.title: [new task]

fields.value:
**How this works.** Opening this issue starts the relay agent (collaborators with write access only).
- **Phase A, design review (no GPU):** it reads your paper and code, checks that the repo installs and the data downloads, and replies with a design doc or with targeted questions.
- **Phase B, build + pilot:** after you reply `go`, it builds the task and pilots two baselines at reduced scale, then opens a PR.
- **Phase C, full measurement:** after another `go`, it measures every baseline on every setting and runs the final checks.

You get an @mention (an email by default) whenever it needs you. Reply in the issue to answer or to give `go`. This issue maps to exactly one pull request (opened in Phase B, updated in Phase C, `Closes #<this issue>`).

**Only the research question and the source paper(s) are required.** Leave any other field blank and the agent proposes it from the paper(s) and the authors' code in its design review; you confirm or edit it before anything is built.

**The rules a task must meet:** one atomic research question that is a paper's own; at least 3 settings from the papers' own protocol (real checkpoints, data and benchmarks, no toy scales; the settings must genuinely differ); published baselines with code; an editable surface that is one algorithmic component; everything downloadable at build time, because compute is offline.

fields.label: Research question
fields.description:
The one atomic ML-science question, and why it matters.
Example: "Which per-token advantage should on-policy distillation use when the teacher is weaker than the student? Matters because OPD is now standard for reasoning models and the usual reverse-KL signal collapses in that regime."

fields.label: Source paper(s)
fields.description:
arXiv / DOI links. The question must be the paper's own research question.
Example: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649 (GKD, Agarwal et al. 2024), Sec. 4 'on-policy distillation'"

fields.label: Codebase
fields.description:
Optional — leave blank and the agent will propose one from the paper(s).
Repository URL + commit or branch (preferably the paper authors' own, small repo), and the entry point that trains / evaluates.
Example: "https://github.com/kiryor/nnPUlearning @ 1a2b3c4, entry point: train.py (trains and reports test error)"

fields.label: Evaluation settings
fields.description:
Optional — leave blank and the agent will propose one from the paper(s).
At least 3, each from the papers' own protocol: model / dataset / budget, plus the metric(s) and direction. Real checkpoints, data and benchmarks, no toy scales; the settings must genuinely differ.
Example (one row per setting):
| setting | model | dataset | budget | metric (direction) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mnist-evenodd | 6-layer MLP | MNIST even/odd | 100 epochs | test error (lower is better) |
| cifar10-vehicle | 13-layer CNN | CIFAR-10 vehicle/animal | 200 epochs | test error (lower is better) |
| 20news | 5-layer MLP on GloVe | 20 Newsgroups | 50 epochs | test error (lower is better) |

fields.label: Baselines
fields.description:
Optional — leave blank and the agent will propose one from the paper(s).
Published methods with code: name, paper, repo@commit. Say which one is the STARTER (the default the agent begins from).
Example:
- uPU (starter): du Plessis et al. 2015, https://github.com/kiryor/nnPUlearning@1a2b3c4 (loss=upu)
- nnPU: Kiryo et al. 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.00593, same repo (loss=nnpu)
- Dist-PU: Zhao et al. 2022, https://github.com/Ray-rui/Dist-PU-Positive-Unlabeled-Learning-from-a-Label-Distribution-Perspective@main

fields.label: Editable scope
fields.description:
Optional — leave blank and the agent will propose one from the paper(s).
Which files / functions / regions the agent may edit, and what stays fixed (data, eval, training loop, budget).
Example: "Editable: the `pu_risk(...)` function in custom_pu.py (the risk estimator). Fixed: data loading and splits, the model, optimizer and epochs, the evaluation."

fields.label: Compute budget
fields.description:
Optional — leave blank and the agent will propose one from the paper(s).
GPUs per setting and wall time per setting. (The agent itself gets 5 h in total.)
Example: "1 x H100 per setting, about 20 min per setting per seed; 3 seeds."

fields.label: Data and weights
fields.description:
Optional. Where datasets and checkpoints come from (URLs, Hugging Face ids), with sizes if known.
Example: "torchvision MNIST / CIFAR-10; 20 Newsgroups via sklearn; GloVe 6B 300d (https://nlp.stanford.edu/data/glove.6B.zip, 822 MB)"

fields.label: Integrity concerns
fields.description:
Optional. What the agent must not be able to reach (test labels, the eval script, a generator, cached answers).
Example: "The class prior pi is given to all methods; the agent must not read test labels or change the prior."

fields.label: Acceptance criteria
fields.description:
Optional. What would make the task good: e.g. the published ordering reproduces on every setting, the starter is clearly beaten by the best baseline.
Example: "nnPU < uPU in test error on all three settings, as in the paper's Table 2."

fields.label: Notes
fields.description: Optional. Anything else the agent should know.

change-task.name: Change an existing task
change-task.description: Ask the relay agent to change one existing ML-Relay task (fix, rerun, improve a baseline, tighten a setting). One issue = one task = one PR.
change-task.title: [change]

fields.value: Opening this issue starts the relay agent (collaborators with write access only). It works on **this task only**, reports back here with an @mention (an email by default), and proposes its changes as **one pull request** linked to this issue (`Closes #<this issue>`). To iterate, reply in the issue; the same PR is updated. `/status` and `/stop` also work. A change that touches another task, or shared files (README, site), needs its own issue.

fields.label: Task
fields.description:
The one task to change: its id as listed in dataset.toml (the backend validates it).
Example: "ml-pu-learning-risk"

fields.label: What should change
fields.description:
Concretely, what should be different in the task.
Example: "Rerun the `nnpu` baseline at 5 seeds instead of 3 and update its leaderboard rows."

fields.label: Why
fields.description:
The reason: a bug, a mismatch with the paper, a weak setting, a new result.
Example: "Seed variance on cifar10-vehicle is larger than the gap between nnpu and dist_pu, so the ordering is not resolved."

fields.label: Acceptance criteria
fields.description:
How we will know the change is right.
Example: "5 seeds per setting; the reported std of nnpu on cifar10-vehicle drops below 0.01; the bundle's oracle still scores."

fields.label: Pointers
fields.description:
Optional. Files, lines, papers, earlier issues or runs.
Example: "tests/meta/config.json `seeds`; issue #1."
